headline: High: ctx can observe Claude Code events and filesystem while marker is a local document processor, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks through shared file-based workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and uses filesystem/MCP surfaces, so it can ingest content that marker may have produced into shared documents. marker is a document-processing agent with no isolation guarantees shown, so file-based instruction smuggling is plausible. The pair lacks direct evidence of a shared channel, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF ctx reads marker-generated files from a shared workspace, injection becomes active.
IF marker outputs attacker-controlled text into documents that ctx later parses as instructions, the pathway is exploitable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Strip or escape instruction-like text before ctx ingests documents.
Require provenance tags on files before ctx processes them.
Disable automatic parsing of marker outputs by ctx.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, harness records, graph data, and MCP servers, while marker is a document processor with no filesystem read/write restrictions shown beyond local-only capabilities. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts from ctx can flow into marker outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF ctx and marker share a filesystem or workspace, leakage is possible.
IF marker processes files containing ctx logs or harness records, those contents can be exposed in outputs.
mitigations: Keep ctx logs in a separate directory.
Mount marker on a read-only subset of inputs.
Redact audit/runtime logs before document processing.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries in the orchestrator.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and can use filesystem/MCP-related surfaces, but marker has no write, git, shell, or network capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only document handling versus ctx's broader automation. Because the pair lacks shared mutable-resource evidence, this stays low.
conditions: IF marker is given write access outside its current profile, conflict risk increases.
IF ctx and marker are pointed at the same mutable directory, concurrent edits could collide.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Keep marker read-only.
Serialize any shared-file updates.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe tool events and produce context that marker may consume as document input, creating a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's input. marker is a document-processing system, so it may render or transform ctx-produced text without verification. The absence of explicit validation or provenance controls makes cascading errors plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF marker ingests ctx-generated files without verification, errors can cascade.
IF ctx writes summaries that marker later transforms into documents, mistaken facts can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require source citations on ctx outputs.
Have marker preserve provenance metadata.
Reject ctx outputs lacking validation markers.
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, which can create retention or residency obligations, while marker's profile shows no data classes touched and no special compliance claims. There is no direct evidence of a residency mismatch or regulated data class flow between them, so only a low compliance gap is supported.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs or harness records, retention policy mismatches may matter.
IF marker stores outputs longer than ctx's log-retention policy, compliance drift can occur.
mitigations: Minimize regulated data in shared runs.
Set a short retention window for logs.
Document deletion/export handling for both agents.
Review where outputs are stored.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across the pair.
